Published online:
    August 26, 2026

Geographic focus:
    China, Hong Kong, Brazil, Indonesia (Asia-Pacific / Global Energy)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — H1 2026 financial results
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [NO]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Full-year production target and capex guidance maintained; new exploration blocks secured

Synopsis:
    CNOOC posted record H1 2026 net profit of 85.8B yuan (+23.4% YoY), driven by higher oil prices (avg. $85.49/bbl, +23.6%) linked to the Iran war, and record production of 398.7M boe (+3.7%). Revenue rose 20% to 206.1B yuan. All-in costs edged up to $29.70/boe. Full-year production guidance of 780–800M boe and capex of 112–122B yuan were maintained. New discoveries in Bohai Bay and Pearl River Mouth Basin, plus new exploration blocks in Brazil and Indonesia, signal active reserve growth. Record interim dividend declared at HK$0.94/share. HK-listed shares up 17% YTD, outperforming Sinopec.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US stock market pricing?
Relevance: IMPLICIT — CNOOC's results reflect elevated oil prices tied to the Iran war, which is a global macro input relevant to US energy prices, inflation expectations, and indirectly to Fed policy and equity market sentiment. No direct US economic data referenced.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 30 — Strong Chinese NOC earnings in a high-oil-price environment are broadly expected given the Iran war context. The magnitude of outperformance and record metrics add marginal new information, but no major surprises.

Q03. Is the content explicitly about bullish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: NO
Impact score: 15 — Indirectly mildly bullish for US energy sector equities (XLE, oil majors) given the high realised oil price signal, but no direct US market bullish catalyst is stated.

Q04. Is the content explicitly about bearish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: NO
Impact score: 20 — Elevated oil prices sustaining at ~$85/bbl, underpinned by the Iran war, carry an implicit bearish undertone for the broader US equity market (NQ/ES) via higher input costs, inflation stickiness, and potential pressure on Fed rate cut expectations.
